headline: Bill placed to abolish RAB and form SRB as replacement
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) will replace the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) under a new law proposed in parliament.
details: A bill was placed in the Jatiya Sangsad yesterday to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish a new elite force called the Special Response Battalion (SRB).

The proposed law states that all manpower, assets, funds, and records of RAB will be transferred to the SRB. Until new regulations are framed, existing 2005 rules regarding disciplinary measures and court proceedings will remain in force.

Under the bill, SRB will function as a specialised unit under the police force, staffed by police officers and members of disciplined forces. It will have its own flag, emblem, and uniform, led by a director general of the rank of additional inspector general of police or above.

The SRB will be empowered to investigate criminal offences and conduct searches, arrests, and seizures. A multi-stakeholder grievance redress committee will be formed to handle public complaints and internal grievances.

The move sparked a debate in parliament, with Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam and Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman demanding detailed discussions. Nahid Islam called RAB a 'symbol of fascism' and cited enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed defended the proposal, stating that the new unit will ensure accountability and transparency, with a dedicated body for investigation and trial that did not exist before.
The bill has been sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs for scrutiny and is expected to return a report within four working days.

headline_marked: 15,717 children reported missing in 7 months: [[2,038 remain untraced]]
headline: 15,717 children reported missing in 7 months: 2,038 remain untraced
summary: Police Headquarters (PHQ) reports that 13,679 children were rescued or returned to their families between January and July this year.
details: A total of 15,717 children were reported missing across Bangladesh between January and July this year, according to Police Headquarters (PHQ).
Of the total missing reports, 13,679 children were rescued or returned to their families, while 2,038 children remain untraced.
The untraced children account for 13 percent of the total number of missing reports filed during this seven-month period.
Data shows that 15,243 children aged between 10 and 17 years were reported missing, with 1,970 remaining untraced.
For children aged zero to nine years, 474 were reported missing, with 68 remaining untraced.
PHQ noted that the number of general diaries (GDs) for missing persons has increased significantly following the introduction of online GD services.
Police data reveals a rising trend in missing person reports: 17,808 GDs were filed in 2023, 16,414 in 2024, and 22,550 in 2025.
caption:

A total of 15,717 children were reported missing across Bangladesh between January and July this year, according to Police Headquarters (PHQ).

Of the total missing reports, 13,679 children were rescued or returned to their families, while 2,038 children remain untraced.

The untraced children account for 13 percent of the total number of missing reports filed during this seven-month period.

Data shows that 15,243 children aged between 10 and 17 years were reported missing, with 1,970 remaining untraced.

For children aged zero to nine years, 474 were reported missing, with 68 remaining untraced.

PHQ noted that the number of general diaries (GDs) for missing persons has increased significantly following the introduction of online GD services.

Police data reveals a rising trend in missing person reports: 17,808 GDs were filed in 2023, 16,414 in 2024, and 22,550 in 2025.
